title: Microsoft Purview retention: what is kept, what is deleted and who decides
summary: Two automation entries create policy containers without setting the controls their rows describe. The retention-action entry needs a narrower description, and the label-publishing entry needs the command that actually publishes a label.

claims.claim: The Purview retention-policy creation entry is Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
2. Select New retention policy

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy with ExchangeLocation and SharePointLocation configures both policy locations and whether the policy retains, deletes or both.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies).
claims.fix: Narrow controls[0].governs, and the corresponding rendered row, to 'Which locations a retention policy covers'. Keep its current call and its note that New-RetentionComplianceRule is required. The printed call sets locations, not the retention action.

claims.claim: Copilot retention policies are created through Purview > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
2. Select New retention policy

claims.claim: The policy guide documents Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -Applications "User:M365Copilot" to add Copilot interactions.
claims.quote: To add Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions to an existing retention policy for newer locations ... Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity “<policy name>” -Applications "User:M365Copilot"

claims.claim: Retention labels are created at Purview > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Retention labels > Create a label.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Retention labels.
2. Select Create a label

claims.claim: New-ComplianceTag supports Name, RetentionAction Keep, RetentionDuration in days and RetentionType ModificationAgeInDays to create a retention label.
claims.quote: New-ComplianceTag -Name "HR Content" -RetentionAction Keep -RetentionDuration 1825 -RetentionType ModificationAgeInDays

claims.claim: Labels are published at Purview > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Label policies > Publish labels.
claims.quote:
If you're using data lifecycle management: Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Label policies
2. Select Publish labels

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -SharePointLocation <site-url> publishes or auto-applies retention labels.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies).
claims.fix: Set controls[3].governs to 'Publishing retention labels to locations' and replace its call with 'New-RetentionComplianceRule -Policy "<policy name>" -PublishComplianceTag "<label name>"'. Set its docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-retentioncompliancerule?view=exchange-ps. Replace its note with 'Publishes an existing label through an existing policy scoped to the required locations.' Update the rendered row identically. The reference states that PublishComplianceTag specifies the published label and makes it visible in apps.

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes are created at Purview > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes.
2. On the Adaptive scopes page, select + Create scope.

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <name> -LocationType User -RawQuery <query> creates a user adaptive scope.
claims.quote:
New-AdaptiveScope
    -Name <String>
    -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType>
    -RawQuery <String>

claims.claim: The Preservation Lock guide documents no UI route for enabling the lock; the row explicitly acknowledges conflicting checkbox documentation.
claims.quote: You must use PowerShell if you need to use Preservation Lock. ... enabling this feature is not available in the UI to safeguard against accidental configuration.

claims.claim: Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" -RestrictiveRetention $true enables Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" -RestrictiveRetention $true

claims.claim: Selecting a policy on the Purview retention policies page displays its distribution status.
claims.quote: You can always check the distribution status of the retention policy by selecting it from the Retention policies page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" -DistributionDetail | Format-List retrieves detailed policy information with accurate distribution and location values.
claims.quote:
Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "Regulation 123 Compliance" -DistributionDetail | Format-List
```

This example displays detailed information ... including accurate values for the DistributionStatus and *Location properties.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: A newly created retention policy is not valid until a rule is added with New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies). For more information, see New-RetentionComplianceRule.

claims.quote: Administrators won't be able to disable or delete these policies after the preservation lock is applied.

claims.claim: Get-RegulatoryComplianceUI's reference describes a preservation-lock checkbox, in conflict with the lock guide.
claims.quote: whether the preservation lock checkbox is displayed for retention policies and the immutable label checkbox is displayed for retention labels

claims.claim: RestrictiveRetention returned by Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy indicates whether Preservation Lock is set.
claims.quote:
Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<Name of Policy>" |Fl
```

You should see RestrictiveRetention is set to True.

claims.quote: If you don't use this switch, the values of the DistributionStatus and *Location property values will be inaccurate.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview retention controls how long Microsoft 365 content is retained and when it is permanently deleted.
claims.quote: Retain and then delete: Retain content for a specified period of time and then permanently delete it.

claims.claim: Retention policies assign common retention settings at the mailbox, site or container level.
claims.quote: assigning the same retention settings at the container level to be automatically inherited by content in that container

claims.claim: Retention labels assign retention settings at the item level, including folders, documents and emails.
claims.quote: use a retention label to assign retention settings at an item level (folder, document, email).

claims.claim: Retention settings use retain and delete actions.
claims.quote:
Managing content commonly requires two actions:

| Action | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Retain content | Prevent permanent deletion and remain available for eDiscovery |
| Delete content | Permanently delete content from your organization |

claims.claim: Retain-only is a supported retention outcome.
claims.quote: Retain-only: Retain content forever or for a specified period of time.

claims.claim: Delete-only is a supported retention outcome.
claims.quote: Delete-only: Permanently delete content after a specified period of time.

claims.claim: Retain and then delete is a supported retention outcome.
claims.quote: Retain and then delete: Retain content for a specified period of time and then permanently delete it.

claims.claim: Content subject to retention remains in place.
claims.quote: When content has retention settings assigned to it, that content remains in its original location.

claims.claim: When retained content is edited or deleted, a copy is automatically retained.
claims.quote: if they edit or delete content that's included in the retention policy, a copy of the content is automatically retained.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive retained copies are stored in the Preservation Hold library.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive sites: The copy is retained in the Preservation Hold library.

claims.claim: Exchange mailbox retained copies are stored in Recoverable Items.
claims.quote: For Exchange mailboxes: The copy is retained in the Recoverable Items folder.

claims.claim: Teams, Viva Engage, Copilot and AI-app retained copies use a hidden SubstrateHolds folder.
claims.quote: For Teams, Viva Engage messages, Copilot and AI apps: The copy is retained in a hidden folder named SubstrateHolds as a subfolder in the Exchange Recoverable Items folder.

claims.claim: Policy retention settings do not travel with content moved outside their container.
claims.quote: the retention settings don't travel with the content in its new location. If that's required, use retention labels instead of retention policies.

claims.claim: Label retention settings travel with content moved within the Microsoft 365 tenant.
claims.quote: retention settings from retention labels travel with the content if it's moved to a different location within your Microsoft 365 tenant.

claims.claim: Retention policies apply automatically rather than through manual item labeling.
claims.quote: retention policies automatically apply to all items at the container level

claims.claim: Retention labels can be applied manually.
claims.quote: Enable people in your organization to apply a retention label manually to content in Outlook and Outlook on the web, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Policies have adaptive or static scopes.
claims.quote: When you create a retention policy or retention label policy, you must choose between adaptive and static to define the scope of the policy.

claims.claim: Adaptive scope membership is evaluated daily using a query against selected attributes.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify ... running daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected locations.

claims.claim: Static scopes cover a whole location or specified inclusions and exclusions.
claims.quote: A static scope doesn't use queries ... it can apply to all instances for a specified location, or use inclusion and exclusions for specific instances for that location.

claims.claim: Retention takes precedence over permanent deletion, subject to the page's separately stated Priority cleanup exception.
claims.quote: By default, retention always takes precedence over permanent deletion ... unless it's subject to priority cleanup

claims.claim: The longest retention period for an item wins.
claims.quote: the content is retained until the end of the longest retention period for the item.

claims.claim: A retention label's delete action takes precedence over a retention policy's delete action.
claims.quote: a delete action from a retention label always takes precedence over a delete action from any retention policy.

claims.claim: For deletion conflicts between policies, adaptive or specifically included scopes take precedence over org-wide static scopes.
claims.quote: an adaptive scope or a static scope that includes specific instances ... takes precedence over a static scope that is configured for all instances for the same location.

claims.claim: Remaining policy deletion conflicts are resolved by the shortest deletion period.
claims.quote: The shortest deletion period wins. Applicable to determine when items will be deleted from retention policies and the outcome couldn't be resolved from the previous level
